system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Project Kestrel: Seller update vs. Buyer playbook (16 issues)**

Seller labels such as "key negotiated positions," "agreed," and "fair and balanced" are assertions, not confirmed authority. No fallback is cleared: Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback, so every recommendation below counters the Seller at our starting position unless noted.

| ID | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1) | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 | **Reject; counter at 25%.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback and needs Frost's written authority identifying the draft, which we don't have. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, recoverable only above the basket (cl 12.2) | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | **Reject; counter at playbook figures.** The Seller's numbers are five times our thresholds and convert the basket into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months, with a "limitation applies to all Claims" override (cl 12.3/13) | 24 months after Completion; limitation applies to general claims only | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval, and the cross-application would drag title and fraud claims into the general regime. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits "for simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject.** Title and capacity are fundamental risks and cannot sit under a 20% cap and 18-month window. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | No express carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | **Reject; insert an express carve-out.** The "any nature" wording would catch fraud, and no one may waive this protection. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | **Reject.** Whole-data-room disclosure would let the Seller disclose away any warranty claim, and the disclosure letter itself says it limits nothing. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Buyer has no claim for any matter it or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3) | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | **Reject; delete.** Constructive knowledge of the data room would gut the warranties and indemnities we are relying on. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2: no final consent or evidence of conditions | Effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | **Reject; make it a pre-Completion condition.** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and the consent and its conditions are not yet satisfied. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion (cl 2/7). DL 3: not repaid, no discharge | Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | **Reject; require payout at Completion.** A post-Completion release leaves our acquired company exposed to a secured lender we have not paid off. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses | DD-005 AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow; on-costs not addressed (DL 5) | Specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded; triggered on-costs included; funds flow must not silently exclude them | **Reject; add a specific line item or Seller funding, including on-costs.** Leaving them out of the funds flow means we could inherit a liability the price doesn't reflect. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or assignment | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure (cl 7.3 conditional transfer); AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way | **Reject; broaden and preserve the SOW3 cure.** The narrow indemnity leaves the Project Materials transfer conditional on payments we can't yet verify. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6: not confirmed as a breach; scope and notification unknown | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates | **Counter; require investigation and updates, do not accept the materiality view.** The Seller's materiality conclusion is unsupported, and the ~1,240-record scope and access question are still open. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals | Three renewals, AUD 330,000 aggregate, "ordinary-course operating costs" (DL 8) | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | **Assess; no price change yet.** The DL doesn't say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, so the ordinary-course label is an assertion. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Tax, IP, title and warranty positions all collapsed into "the general regime" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** Folding these into the general regime would silently apply the 20% cap and 18-month window to fundamental and specific risks. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 (DL 10) | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof | **Reject as sufficient; require independent evidence.** The register is the Seller's own document, so it cannot verify title on its own. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax/IP open terms | Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP remain open; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | **Reject; keep open.** The Seller's claim that these are settled is unsupported and would place them under the general cap and time limit. |

**Process points**

- **Stale facts.** The disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Refresh the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus, incident and renewal facts before the mark-up goes out. I have not verified any of these facts independently.
- **Authority.** Only Amelia Frost can approve the 20% cap, the 18-month period or any Riverlark post-Completion release, and she must do so in writing identifying the draft. None is on file.
- **Fraud and title.** Neither the fraud carve-out nor the separate title regime appears in the Seller's draft, so both should be inserted expressly rather than negotiated down from the Seller's language.
=== END ADVICE ===
